messages.subject: geom_segment to edge of graph with scale_x_log10()
parts:
I posted this a couple of years ago, with no response. Thought I'd try it again:

I want to plot a curve with log x axis, and identify particular points on the curve by drawing a horizontal line out to the curve from the left border of the plot, then dropping a vertical down to the border of the graph. For untransformed axes, setting x to -Inf does just what I want, but, I guess, since log(-Inf) = NaN, the horizontal line is not drawn with scale_x_log10(). Is there another way to do this?

Woody

On 9/3/2014 10:01 AM, Woody Setzer wrote:
> I posted this a couple of years ago, with no response. Thought I'd try it
> again:
Well, I certainly can't fault you for being too eager to repost.

> I want to plot a curve with log x axis, and identify particular points on
> the curve by drawing a horizontal line out to the curve from the left
> border of the plot, then dropping a vertical down to the border of the
> graph. For untransformed axes, setting x to -Inf does just what I want,
> but, I guess, since log(-Inf) = NaN, the horizontal line is not drawn with
> scale_x_log10(). Is there another way to do this?
>
> Woody

A trick that seems to work is to set the left edge at 0, which on a log
scale will be transformed to -Inf

Here is an example using the mtcars data, and drawing a line to the
left-most point:

# get a set of target points, one for each line
start_points <- ddply(mtcars, .(cyl), function(DF) {
DF[DF$wt == min(DF$wt),]
})

ggplot(mtcars, aes(x=wt, y=mpg, colour=factor(cyl))) +
geom_point() +
geom_line() +
geom_segment(data=start_points, aes(xend = wt, y=mpg, yend=mpg), x=0) +
scale_x_log10()


--
